## What we must prove

::: {.lead}
The KPIs were presented yesterday. Each one needs a kind of evidence.
:::

| Objective | Evidence we collect | Task |
|:-------|:-----------------------|:-------|
| O1 Orchestration | The same service built manually and with agents, plus stress-test logs | T6.3, T6.4 |
| O2 Federation | Query and mapping benchmarks across sites, onboarding time of a new source | T6.4, all pilots |
| O3 Explainability | Audit-trail checks, operator surveys, agreement with expert logic | T6.2, T6.1, T6.4 |
| O4 Demonstration | Planning time, hosting capacity and congestion estimates, independent review | T6.1, T6.2 |

::: {.notes}
Timing for the whole session (40 minutes, 10:45 to 11:25): about 22 minutes of slides, 10 minutes of discussion, 8 minutes of buffer. The cross-WP alignment follows at 11:25 and the day ends at 12:00.
Start by naming what carries over from yesterday: the KPI framework in WP3, the pilot contacts, the data inventory dates. Update this note with the decisions taken on day 1.
Key sentence: WP6 produces the evidence for all four objectives.
Likely question: who decides if a target is met? A partner who did not run the pilot reviews the results, and the objective audit at M36 closes it.
:::

## What TRL 5 means here

::: {.quad}
::: {}
<b>Relevant environment</b>
Real data where we have it, simulated grid constraints, lab or simulated settings. Live grid control is TRL 6 and outside the project.
:::
::: {}
<b>Shadow mode</b>
Recommendations run beside human decisions. Nothing controls a physical asset.
:::
::: {}
<b>One KPI framework</b>
Every pilot uses the scorecard from D3.2, so results compare across use cases and countries.
:::
::: {}
<b>Degraded mode</b>
We test lost data, broken links and bad input on purpose.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Key sentence: validated at TRL 5 means it works in a relevant environment beside people, not that it runs the grid.
Likely question: why not TRL 6? The proposal scopes the project to TRL 5 and says live demonstrations are out of scope.
:::

## How each use case is evaluated

::: {.cols}
::: {.col .ecp}
<span class="tag">ECP</span>

Historical planning cases first, then planning with emerging communities. Compared with expert plans.

Measures: planning time, accuracy, usability for non-experts, correct national rules.
:::
::: {.col .edcr}
<span class="tag">EDCR</span>

Replay of past events, live shadow mode, review sessions with operators. Compared with operator decisions.

Measures: acceptance, agreement, transparency, time to decision, audit trail.
:::
::: {.col .esla}
<span class="tag">ESLA</span>

The same services built the conventional way and with the toolbox.

Measures: person-hours, elapsed time, workflow errors, share of steps without a human.
:::
:::

::: {.callout}
T6.4 runs beside all three: load, fault injection, bad data, guardrail and oversight tests.
:::

::: {.notes}
Each task leader writes the protocol for their pilot. KTH checks that it follows the D3.2 framework.
Likely question: who recruits the users? The pilot hosts, with a mix of ages, backgrounds and genders. Usability data is sex-disaggregated, as the proposal promises.
:::

## Backup: evaluation design by use case {.smaller}

| | ECP | EDCR | ESLA |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Cases and data | Historical cases per country, then emerging communities in Italy and simulated ones in Austria | Building and community data via ProptechOS, grid constraints informed by the DSO, historical events for replay | One or two reference services, such as a demand forecast and a demand-response algorithm |
| Baseline | Time and cost of conventional planning | Operator decisions in past events | Conventional development process, measured first |
| Comparison | AI plan against expert plan | AI recommendation against operator decision, guardrail result recorded | Same service, automated against conventional |
| Users | Community managers and members, including non-experts | Operators and DSO staff | Developers and service operators |
| Indicators | Planning time, accuracy, task completion, understanding of explanations, correct national rules | Acceptance, agreement, trust, time to decision, guardrail interventions, audit trail completeness | Person-hours, elapsed time, errors and reruns, autonomy rate, compliance trail |
| Report | D6.1 | D6.2 | D6.3 |

## Backup: robustness test catalogue (T6.4) {.smaller}

| Test family | Examples | Metric |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Load | 10, 50 and 100 virtual communities, 100 or more concurrent agents | Response time, throughput, error rate |
| Federation latency | Cross-site SPARQL queries, with and without edge caching | Share of queries under 2 s (target 90%), mapping under 500 ms |
| Fault injection | Data source down, stale data, link loss, agent crash, failed grid simulation | Recovery time, fallback behaviour |
| Data quality | Missing values, outliers, wrong units, conflicting sources | Detection rate, false alarms |
| Guardrail and oversight | Recommendations that break voltage or capacity limits, low-confidence cases, manual override | Violations rejected (100%), escalation rate, guardrail latency under 100 ms |
| Security | Role-based access checks, unauthorised tool use | Policy violations blocked |

## Backup: roles and meetings {.smaller}

| Role | Who | Responsibility |
|:--|:--|:--|
| WP leader | KTH | Plan, coordination, consistent evaluation, final reports |
| Task leaders | UNICA (T6.1), KTH (T6.2, T6.4), AIT (T6.3) | Protocols, execution, task reports |
| Pilot coordinators | One named person per pilot | Site access, participants, local logistics, data agreements |
| Evaluation lead | One person at KTH | KPI data sheets, analysis, cross-case evaluation |
| Reviewers | A partner who did not run the pilot | Independent check of the results |

Meetings: monthly WP6 call from M16, fortnightly from M26, a pilot readiness review before M30. Each pilot protocol is approved before data collection starts. Problems found in the beta go to WP5 with a severity, and a fix freeze date comes before the final measurements.

## Backup: risks for WP6 {.smaller}

| Risk | Mitigation |
|:--|:--|
| Unstable access to data | Data access agreements early, readiness check at M26, synthetic data as fallback |
| Pilot users lose interest | Community managers at each site, clear benefits, gamified feedback in the toolboxes |
| Platform does not scale | Simulated load tests in T6.4, modular microservices |
| Regulation changes | Monitoring in T2.2, reconfigurable regulatory guardrails |
| Explanations too technical | Trust-Score tracking in WP6, iterative UI testing in WP5 |
| The beta arrives late and shortens the pilot period | Alpha demos at M24, dry run at M26, protocols and tooling ready before M30 |
| Operators have little time for shadow-mode sessions | Agree a schedule with EIN and the DSO early, replay historical events, short sessions |
| No baselines, so no improvement can be shown | Measure baselines from M16 |
| Ethics and privacy approvals take long | Prepare protocols at M18 to M22, check national requirements |
